title: Trump: Roy Cohn dies from AIDS after Donald Trump ditches him
description_short: Trump: Roy Cohn dies from AIDS after Donald Trump ditches him
description_medium: Roy Cohn, the lawyer and mentor who advised Donald Trump on business and legal matters, died from AIDS-related illness on August 2, 1986, at age 59. Accounts in the supplied record say Cohn and Trump had grown distant and had not spoken for months. Cohn publicly described his illness as liver cancer; Trump attended his funeral. The record does not establish why their relationship ended.
description_long: Roy Cohn, a lawyer known for his role as counsel to Senator Joseph McCarthy, died on August 2, 1986, at age 59. He had become an adviser and mentor to Donald Trump, offering guidance on Trump’s business and legal affairs. The supplied timeline says that their relationship had deteriorated before Cohn’s death and that Trump moved legal work to other attorneys after learning Cohn was ill. Cohn’s secretary, Susan Bell, reportedly said the two men had not spoken for months; the record does not establish the date or circumstances of their last conversation. Cohn publicly said he had liver cancer, while the reported cause of death was AIDS-related illness. Trump attended the funeral. These accounts document a close professional association followed by reported estrangement, but do not establish that Trump deliberately abandoned Cohn or explain why their contact ended. The headline’s word “ditches” is therefore a characterization rather than a demonstrated fact about the cause of their separation.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Roy Cohn dies from AIDS after Donald Trump ditches him
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Roy Cohn dies from AIDS after Donald Trump ditches him

notes: The New York Times link returned HTTP 403. The supplied timeline and draft report the professional relationship and estrangement; they do not establish the reason or exact timing of the break. The description treats “ditches” as a headline characterization.
proposed_correction: Consider changing “ditches him” to “relationship had deteriorated” unless reporting establishes that Trump deliberately ended the relationship because of Cohn’s illness.

title: Trump blames Wilbur Ross for being so close to bankruptcy
description_short: Trump blames Wilbur Ross for being so close to bankruptcy
description_medium: On November 13, 1990, Trump ended negotiations with Trump Taj Mahal bondholders over a proposal for him to assume more debt as he sought to avoid bankruptcy. In his statement, he blamed Wilbur Ross, who represented the bondholders and later became Trump’s Commerce secretary. The supplied account does not include the statement’s full text, the proposed terms, or the bondholders’ response.

preserved_fields.title: Trump blames Wilbur Ross for being so close to bankruptcy
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump blames Wilbur Ross for being so close to bankruptcy

notes: The linked New York Times article returned HTTP 403. The packet truncates Trump’s statement and lacks the debt terms, bondholders’ response, and outcome of this negotiation, so its effect on the Taj Mahal’s finances cannot be described reliably.
proposed_correction: Add the full statement, proposed restructuring terms, bondholders’ response, and eventual outcome from contemporaneous reporting before drawing conclusions about Ross’s role or the financial consequences.

title: Trump: The Senate confirms Mogilevich Organization operates in the USA
description_short: Trump: The Senate confirms Mogilevich Organization operates in the USA
description_medium: A May 1996 Senate hearing addressed Russian organized crime in the United States. CNN reported that senators were told Russian criminal groups were gaining a U.S. foothold. The available report does not establish that the Senate confirmed the presence of Semion Mogilevich’s organization, identify testimony about his group, or connect the hearing to Donald Trump.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: The Senate confirms Mogilevich Organization operates in the USA
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: The Senate confirms Mogilevich Organization operates in the USA

notes: The CNN report’s headline describes warnings about Russian criminal groups, not a formal Senate finding about the Mogilevich organization. The hearing transcript, witnesses, evidence and any committee conclusion are not in the packet, and the record does not establish a Trump connection.
proposed_correction: Replace the title with a neutral description of the hearing topic unless the transcript establishes testimony about Mogilevich’s organization; remove the Trump framing and classify only if a supported connection and fitting category are established.

title: Complete Constitutional Order Collapse - Rule of Law Final Termination
description_short: Complete Constitutional Order Collapse - Rule of Law Final Termination
description_medium: The Guardian reported that courts temporarily blocked Trump’s birthright-citizenship order and federal spending freeze; the administration later rescinded the freeze. Legal scholars cited in the article argued that these actions exceeded presidential authority. The disputes show serious conflicts over executive power, but not the complete collapse of constitutional government claimed in the existing title.
description_long: In a February 1, 2025 report, the Guardian described several early Trump administration actions that historians and legal scholars said violated the Constitution or federal law. The examples included an order restricting birthright citizenship and a freeze on federal spending. A federal judge temporarily blocked the citizenship order, while another judge suspended the spending freeze after lawsuits challenged it under the Constitution and the Impoundment Control Act. The administration rescinded the freeze two days after announcing it. The article reported that the pause disrupted programs including Medicaid payments, childcare, senior meals, housing subsidies and special education. It also described the firing of inspectors general and removal of members of the National Labor Relations Board and Equal Employment Opportunity Commission before their terms ended. Laurence Tribe and Erwin Chemerinsky criticized the administration’s approach; those are attributed legal assessments, not final judgments on every action. The reporting documents disputes and temporary judicial checks, including the withdrawal of the spending freeze. It does not establish that courts or Congress ceased functioning, that constitutional rights were eliminated, or that the United States had entered permanent authoritarian rule.
subcategory: Executive Power and Rule of Law

preserved_fields.title: Complete Constitutional Order Collapse - Rule of Law Final Termination
preserved_fields.description_short: Complete Constitutional Order Collapse - Rule of Law Final Termination

notes: Replaced the unsupported claim of completed constitutional collapse with the Guardian’s reported executive actions, litigation and temporary court orders. The article attributes constitutional assessments to legal scholars.
proposed_correction: Replace the title’s claim of total collapse with a description of the specific executive actions and legal challenges reported.

title: Trump World Tower opens, uses mafia to sell condos to Russia
description_short: Trump World Tower opens, uses mafia to sell condos to Russia
description_medium: Bloomberg reported that Russian and neighboring-country buyers purchased many Trump World Tower units. Broker Dolly Lenz estimated that she sold about 65 apartments to Russian buyers, and the report said regional buyers owned roughly a third of units on upper floors by 2004. It also described Moscow marketing and German-bank financing; it did not establish that a criminal group brokered the sales.
description_long: Trump World Tower opened in Manhattan in 2001. A 2017 Bloomberg investigation reported that wealthy buyers from Russia and neighboring countries purchased apartments in the building. Real-estate broker Dolly Lenz estimated that she sold about 65 units to Russian buyers, while the report said people or companies with regional ties owned roughly one-third of units on floors 76 through 83 by 2004. Bloomberg also described marketing in Moscow and financing tied to German banks. The report’s figures are estimates and ownership research, not a complete ledger of purchasers. Some buyers had faced allegations or investigations involving organized crime or money laundering, but those cases concerned individual buyers. The reporting supplied here does not show that a mafia organization arranged the sales, that Trump or his company knowingly worked with such a group, or that criminal proceeds financed the building. The record can support an account of international sales and marketing, with the numbers attributed to Bloomberg and Lenz. Its headline’s claim that Trump “uses mafia” to sell apartments needs separate evidence and should not be presented as established fact.

preserved_fields.title: Trump World Tower opens, uses mafia to sell condos to Russia
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump World Tower opens, uses mafia to sell condos to Russia

notes: The supplied Bloomberg summary supports Russian-buyer estimates, Moscow marketing and German-bank financing, but not criminal-group brokerage. It does not provide a complete buyer ledger or show Trump’s knowledge of buyers’ alleged conduct.
proposed_correction: Change the title to describe Bloomberg’s reporting on Russian and regional buyers unless evidence establishes that a criminal organization brokered sales or that Trump knowingly used it.
